### 2026-10-30: After I had finished up with the schematics initially, I tried to route everything.

**4h**

After I had finished up with the schematics initially, I tried to route everything.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/19ec467685fcc7d61e9a331ca6241c6036429a553d36ac38e7a9750d8f747d51.png)

Didn't quite look right to me though, and I also noticed that there were significantly more parts listed on the guide, so I decided to go back to the schematics.

I first wanted to work on the connector.
I looked over some more resources, and eventually decided that it'd be better off to just stick with a 01x09 connector as opposed to the 01x11. This choice came from the fact that I was initially connecting all of the pins, but moving to the 01x09 allowed me to only add the pins I needed, and the extra pin to connect the SD card reader.
I also added in the labels for the pins.

 (I'm not certain, but I'm pretty sure that Ki-cad automatically makes those lines and allows connections whenever the labels are the same? I'll definitely find time to learn as much as possible about the software later. )

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/znPqAmwpqKgcRf4K4bX1PsOPu2V8arf1/5d45da94912abeceb3603de02d8499d7966850b863c6071d8d02ce854688a446.png)

After that, I initially thought that I'd add a blueprint for the TFT screen to the connector, but after looking at the list of blueprints, I realized that I didn't have to worry about managing the screen in the first place.

I decided to figure out what else the list was talking about, so I started looking into everything, starting with MOSFETs, which are essentially  a specified transistor for switching and amplification.

I also realized that since I was using an adafruit TFT, I wouldn't have to worry about the MOSFET, since they apparently have built in transistors. (Makes sense, considering the fact that it supposedly constantly risks having too much voltage routed to it.)

I then added no connection symbols to the loose ends on the raspberry pi, to make sure that there were no errors with the PCB schematics. (Not 100% sure if this is a good practice, but I did it anyway :/ )

After that, I decided to call it for the day. Tomorrow, I'll work on the potentiometer and the SD card reader. After that, I MIGHT make some housing for the project. (VERY BIG IF)
